observations: PAL1991 p5 and Plate4 fig9 support the cf. identification,12–15 leaves per whorl,8–10cm length,2mm width, sessile linear entire blades and short narrowed rounded tips. Poor cuticle preservation leaves species attribution uncertain.

Actual model has36 attached linear blades in three separated12-blade whorls.90mm lengths and2mm widths are inside the exact frozen ranges. The full-volume narrow terminal face is not a single-point tip.

The frozen design requires a shallow central groove and implements a0.18mm depression. The only frozen fossil source instead describes a midrib; its plate does not resolve whether a depression should replace that feature. I cannot certify that modeled surface interpretation from the present ledger. This is an evidence gap, not a proved biological absence of grooves.

blockers.issue: The shallow central groove is not demonstrated by the only frozen cf.-fossil reference; do not infer exact fossil surface anatomy from genus familiarity.
blockers.minimal_next_step: Provide a primary-source/pixel basis specifically supporting this cf. reconstruction surface, or produce a transparently derived new revision with evidence-bounded surface interpretation. Preserve the original freeze and cf. limitation; do not silently replace the source or claim uncertainty is a pass.

observations: Selected2014 source supports opposite/subopposite two-ranked narrow blades with blunted apices, no midrib, and a small immature cone on a thickened branch. Whole-crown stature remains artistic, not fossil evidence.

Actual432 leaves are105mm by15mm, aspect ratio approximately7, and have finite blunt terminal edges. These hard dimensions pass; the tree has9 limbs,27 twigs,27 buds and one cone. Final child-base contact tests no longer reproduce the retained early floating-junction failures.

Cone detail shows a broad bare faceted core with small isolated projections rather than the required smooth upturned imbricate scale surface. External-ray sampling confirms all40 scales have some exposed surface, so full burial is NOT claimed. Each top-tier scale has68–69 of70 sample points inside core and only1–2 exposed.

The required transverse growth scar is not visibly represented on the plain fertile support. Rounded terminal buds are simple faceted ellipsoids rather than visibly scaly structures. These are secondary missing identifying details to address with the cone repair.

blockers.issue: Mostly embedded scale geometry leaves a visibly naked core and does not express smooth upturned imbrication; a nonempty or partly exposed scale is not sufficient.
blockers.minimal_next_step: Create a new revision reshaping/exposing the cone scales into a coherent overlapping upturned surface while retaining real support attachment and the intended small cone. Add the frozen growth-scar and scaly-bud detail. Stay within14000tris/1000000bytes/6materials; then measure/contact-check, rebuild twice and re-render the exact final subject.

observations: Used Sun2002 A.sinensis panelsA–D,H,I and Fig3, not liaoningensis panelsE–G,J–L. The source describes dissected leaves, reduced roots, terminal carpels above paired stamens and absence of perianth.

Four slender fertile shoots carry64 carpels and32 paired-stamen stalks/64 anthers in the required ordering;12 genuinely three-level divided leaves have324 distinct ultimate lobes. Swollen bases and sparse1+4 roots are present. Actual whole-object exposed-surface samples exist for every component.

Carpels14mm by1.8mm and anthers4.5mm by0.65mm satisfy exact hard ranges. No enlarged pods, flower cups, petals or sepals. Thin leaf divisions are faint at full-object512px, but top/silhouette and the dedicated divided-leaf detail make the branching readable.

Historical over-budget and detached-leaf attempts remain retained. Final13632tris and907464bytes are under the hard ceilings. Doyle/Endress2014 supports retaining phylogenetic uncertainty; this is not an earliest-angiosperm or definitive habitat claim.
